sections.label: D
sections.title: Circle the correct words.
sections.note: Choose the form that expresses necessity, lack of necessity, or prohibition.

questions.prompt: 1. Hurry! We ___ be at the airport in an hour.
questions.explanation: The deadline creates a necessity, so use have to.

questions.prompt: 2. Shh! Be quiet! You ___ wake the baby.
questions.explanation: Mustn't expresses prohibition: waking the baby is not allowed.

questions.prompt: 3. You ___ remember to call your mother.
questions.explanation: Must expresses a strong obligation to remember.

questions.prompt: 4. I ___ study today because the test was cancelled.
questions.explanation: The cancelled test removes the necessity to study; it does not prohibit studying.

sections.label: E
sections.title: Complete the sentences. Write have to or don't have to.
sections.note: Use have to for necessity and don't have to when something is not necessary.

questions.prompt: 1. I ___ go to school tomorrow. It's Sunday.
questions.explanation: Sunday removes the necessity to go to school, so use don't have to.

questions.prompt: 2. We don't have any milk. I ___ go to the supermarket.
questions.explanation: There is no milk, so going to the supermarket is necessary.

questions.prompt: 3. I broke my smartphone. I ___ get a new one.
questions.explanation: The broken phone creates a practical necessity, so use have to.

questions.prompt: 4. I have money for lunch. You ___ give me any more.
questions.explanation: Because the speaker already has money, giving more is unnecessary.

sections.label: J
sections.title: Write the words in the correct order to make sentences.
sections.note: Use the present perfect and correct punctuation.

questions.prompt: 1. headline / written / the / editor / hasn't / The
answers: The editor hasn't written the headline
The editor has not written the headline
questions.explanation: Use subject + hasn't + past participle + object.

questions.prompt: 2. have / I / test / finished / the
questions.explanation: Use subject + have + past participle + object.

questions.prompt: 3. the / We / problem / discussed / have
questions.explanation: Use subject + have + past participle + object.

questions.prompt: 4. store / hasn't / She / the / gone / to
answers: She hasn't gone to the store
She has not gone to the store
questions.explanation: Gone is the past participle of go, used after hasn't.

sections.label: K
sections.title: Complete the sentences. Write have, has, haven't, or hasn't.
sections.note: Choose the correct present-perfect auxiliary for the subject and meaning.

questions.prompt: 1. I ___ read the article about the old house. Is it interesting?
questions.explanation: The question Is it interesting? shows that the speaker has not read the article, so use haven't.

questions.prompt: 2. ___ she told you about the party?
questions.explanation: She is third-person singular, so a present-perfect question begins with Has.

questions.prompt: 3. We ___ been to that restaurant. It's good!
questions.explanation: We takes have, and the positive comment suggests prior experience.

questions.prompt: 4. The hero from the accident ___ written a book. He'll do it next year.
questions.explanation: He will do it next year, so the book has not been written yet.

sections.label: L

questions.prompt: 1. She ___ ___ dinner.

parts.label: Form of have
parts.explanation: She is third-person singular, so use has.

parts.label: Main verb
parts.explanation: The present perfect requires the past participle eaten, not the simple past ate.

questions.prompt: 2. They ___ ___ the movie.

parts.label: Form of have
parts.explanation: They takes have.

parts.label: Main verb
parts.explanation: The present perfect requires the past participle seen, not the simple past saw.

questions.prompt: 3. I ___ ___ an article before.

parts.label: Form of have
parts.explanation: I takes have.

parts.label: Main verb
parts.explanation: The present perfect requires the past participle written, not the simple past wrote.
